data.title: Phillips 66 and Valero lead S&P energy holdings with 'A' growth grades
data.description:
As we navigate the third quarter of 2026, the S&P Energy sector continues to experience significant macroeconomic headwinds and shifting demand dynamics, making strategic stock selection and growth assessments a primary focus for active market participants.

Below is a list of the top holdings of the S&P Energy sector arranged according to their growth grade. These specific companies are selected because they represent the largest, most influential holdings in the sector by market capitalization, offering a comprehensive look at how the sector's heavyweights are scaling and expanding. Stocks with a grade of B- or above are considered Buys, while those with D+ or below fall into Sell territory.

The list is topped by Phillips 66 (PSX) and Valero Energy Corporation (VLO), both earning an A growth grade along with Strong Buy quant ratings. Marathon Petroleum Corporation (MPC) follows closely with an A- grade and also carries a Strong Buy rating.

The Williams Companies, Inc. (WMB) rounds out the Buy-rated stocks with a B+ growth grade, though it holds only a Hold quant rating. The remaining holdings, ConocoPhillips (COP), Chevron Corporation (CVX), ExxonMobil Holdings Corporation (XOM), EOG Resources, Inc. (EOG), Kinder Morgan, Inc. (KMI), and SLB N.V. (SLB), fall into the Hold or Sell tiers based on their growth grades ranging from C+ down to D-.

The growth factor grade is a quantitative assessment used in stock analysis to evaluate a company's growth prospects and expansion trajectory. This metric systematically analyzes multiple growth-related indicators to determine how effectively a company is scaling its business operations.

Growth factor grades are typically expressed on a letter scale (A+ through F), where higher grades indicate stronger growth characteristics relative to sector peers. An A+ grade represents exceptional growth potential, while lower grades suggest more moderate expansion or potential headwinds.

Here is the list:

  1. Phillips 66 (PSX), Growth grade: A

  2. Valero Energy Corporation (VLO), Growth grade: A

  3. Marathon Petroleum Corporation (MPC), Growth grade: A-

  4. The Williams Companies, Inc. (WMB), Growth grade: B+

  5. ConocoPhillips (COP), Growth grade: C+

  6. Chevron Corporation (CVX), Growth grade: C+

  7. ExxonMobil Holdings Corporation (XOM), Growth grade: C-

  8. EOG Resources, Inc. (EOG), Growth grade: D+

  9. Kinder Morgan, Inc. (KMI), Growth grade: D

  10. SLB N.V. (SLB), Growth grade: D-

Energy ETFs: (XLE), (AMLP), (VDE), (XOP), (OIH), and (IXC)

data.title: Nvidia receives 'top pick' as BMO initiates coverage on array of semiconductor stocks
data.description:
BMO initiated coverage on a range of semiconductor and quantum computing stocks on Thursday, with Nvidia (NVDA) receiving the "top pick" among the group due to its full-stack combination of hardware and software and its dominance in market share.

Nvidia received a $340 price target along with an Outperform rating.

"Next-gen Vera Rubin NVL72 system ramps in 2H," wrote analyst Harsh Kumar in an exhaustive investor report. Stock trades at an 18x forward P/E, a discount considering revenue growth of 84% and 50% in FY27 and FY28, respectively, based on our model. We believe market valuations are mispricing an opportunity given a defensible full systems end-to-end HW/SW moat."

BMO was bullish over several AI-exposed semi stocks, including Broadcom (AVGO), AMD (AMD), Marvell (MRVL) and Semtech (SMTC). These all received Outperform ratings with targets of $455, $550, $250 and $155, respectively.

"We see AVGO as the #2 AI supplier led by custom ASIC (XPU) and networking," Kumar noted. "The AAPL supply agreement has been renewed, while infra software remains mission-critical for enterprises. AMD's Helios joins the full rack market, primed with three lead customers (OpenAI, Meta, Anthropic). MRVL is a top optical PAM4 supplier and is gaining momentum in XPU/XPU-attach and switches. STMC's revenues incrementally step up from ACC/LPO connectivity."

In the analog space, BMO handed out Outperform ratings to Analog Devices (ADI), Impinj (PI) and Microchip Technology (MCHP). They received price targets of $430, $220 and $95, respectively.

"Analog names are emerging from post-COVID correction," Kumar said. "We're seeing positive signals supporting growth in analog. PMI >50, excess channel inventory cleared, book-to-bill above 1, bookings/backlogs starting to grow, and customer expedites are picking up. Industry was the first to recover, while auto showing positive signs. Defense is also solid from geo tensions."

Among quantum, D-Wave (QBTS) earned an Outperform rating and a $35 price target. BMO views the company as one of the best suited for commercial success due to its presence in two leading quantum approaches.

data.title: Wall Street gains ground as yields calm and Bitcoin extends its climb
data.description:
Wall Street’s major market averages were firmly in the green on Friday, as Treasury yields held steady and Bitcoin (BTC-USD) saw sharp swings. 

The blue-chip Dow (DJI) was last +0.7%, the benchmark S&P 500 (SP500) was last +0.3%, and the tech-focused Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) was last +0.2%. 

From a sector-by-sector standpoint, nine of the 11 S&P segments pushed up into the green and were led by materials, while utilities were the worst performer. 

Treasury yields were mostly quiet. The U.S. 2-Year Treasury yield (US2Y) moved up 2 basis point to 4.21%, the U.S. 10-Year Treasury yield (US10Y) was flat at 4.71%, and the U.S. 30-Year Treasury yield (US30Y) ticked up 1 basis point to 5.26%. 

Bitcoin (BTC-USD) is seeing sharp swings Friday as the cryptocurrency extends a volatile rebound from below $64K earlier this week.

“After three weeks of strong performance, the S&P 500 is finally succumbing to the usual August volatility that we tend to see this time of year, driven by rising bond yields and confusion about the Treasury's bond purchase program. Bond yields are on the rise, and don't seem to be responding to the Treasury's purchases, largely because the bond market is massive and is pricing in a stronger economy and higher inflation,” Paul Stanley of Arca stated. 

As for stocks that were on the move, shares of Robinhood Markets (HOOD) climbed higher by +14.6%, while shares of Marvell Technology (MRVL) fell -2.6%.

data.title: Flower Foods misses Q2 estimates, lowers guidance on 'cautious view' for FY26
data.description:
Flowers Foods’ (FLO) latest quarterly results reflected the persistent macroeconomic pressures in the food industry, competitive activity, and higher input costs, all of which caused the company to miss second-quarter expectations.

"Our second quarter results reflect the continued challenges across the fresh packaged bread category,” said Ryals McMullian, CEO of Flowers Foods. “While these headwinds weighed on our performance, they also reinforced the actions we are taking to strengthen our competitiveness and improve execution.” 

The disappointing second-quarter results led the company to lower its outlook for the year to reflect “a more cautious view for the balance of 2026.” Flower Foods (FLO) now expects sales to be down 2.2% to 3.5% to a range of $5.070B to $5.142B, down 2% at the midpoint from the previous range and less than the $5.16B estimate.

FY26 profit is now expected to be within a range of $0.75 to $0.85 per share compared to prior guidance of $0.80 to $0.90 per share. This compares to the consensus estimate of $0.83 per share.  

Because of the inflationary pressure on consumer spending along with higher production costs, Flower Foods (FLO) experienced a 4% decrease in net sales and a 30% drop in profits in the second quarter, both of which were worse than the street expected. Additionally, a key operating income metric was down 19.2%, representing 9.3% of sales, a 180 basis point decrease.

However, the company’s liquidity position improved during the quarter, providing additional funding to “improve performance and better align resources with the opportunities to create the greatest long-term value.” Cash and cash equivalents jumped to $52.8M from $12M at the beginning of the year.

Consistent with the findings in this comprehensive review, Flower Foods (FLO) is taking actions to further align the organization to improve its cost structure.

data.title: Modine stock surges on report naming Google as $4B data center customer
data.description:
Modine Manufacturing (MOD) shares surged 8% on Friday after Hunterbrook said that Google is the unnamed hyperscaler behind the company’s more than $4B long-term capacity agreement announced in May.

Modine had said on May 26 that it signed the agreement through 2029 with an unnamed strategic data center customer for its Airedale by Modine cooling solutions.

Hunterbrook said it found what appeared to be Modine’s internal data center database in a publicly accessible GitHub repository and that the files identified Google as the customer behind the agreement. The report said the database also showed another $4.5B of Google-related cooling demand, with about $433M booked.Modine makes cooling and thermal management equipment used in data centers and other industrial applications.

There is also about $3B of firm or likely commitments from Amazon Web Services, Crusoe, and other data center customers, bringing modeled demand in the database to nearly $23B. AWS accounted for more than half of the total, Hunterbrook said.

data.title: BLS benchmark revision could erase 200K reported jobs, Pantheon Macro warns
data.description:
The Bureau of Labor Statistics will release its preliminary estimate of the 2026 benchmark revision to payrolls next week and economists Samuel Tombs and Oliver Allen at Pantheon Macroeconomics are warning the numbers will reveal significant overstatement in reported job gains.

The firm projects that net job creation was around 200K lower in the 12 months through March 2026 than the establishment survey indicated—a discrepancy attributed almost entirely to structural data collection problems. The benchmark revision compares monthly establishment survey figures against the Quarterly Census of Employment and Wages, which draws on comprehensive unemployment insurance tax records and is considered the gold standard of employment data.

Recent revisions have been sharply negative; last year's preliminary estimate showed payrolls 911K lower than reported for March 2025, eventually revised to -862K. The primary culprit is nonresponse bias: only about 30% of businesses contacted by the BLS now agree to participate in the establishment survey, down from a stable 60%-70% range throughout the 2010s. Businesses refusing to participate tend to be financially weaker than those willing to supply information, creating systematic distortion. 

Two other historical contributors—the birth-death model and counting of unauthorized workers—appear less problematic this cycle, the economists wrote.

The revision carries relevance for Federal Reserve policy deliberations, though the data release appears set to coincide exactly with Chair Warsh's Jackson Hole speech, preventing the numbers from influencing his prepared remarks. Pantheon maintains its forecast that the fed funds mid-point will hold at 3.625% through December 2026.

data.title: Splash Beverage to rename as Endovia Health Sciences; shares up
data.description:
• Splash Beverage (SBEV) will change its corporate name to Endovia Health Sciences and begin trading on NYSE American under ticker EDVA at market open on August 24, 2026.
  • The rebranding marks the Company’s strategic shift from legacy beverage operations toward a diversified cannabinoid-based health sciences platform.
  • Endovia’s strategy focuses on commercial pharmaceutical assets, FDA-regulated human and veterinary therapeutics, and consumer wellness and beverage products.
  • Endovia is advancing CannEpil® through regulated human and veterinary development pathways in the U.S.
  • SBEV shares up 6.6%.
